sentences.text: Macrourogaleus featured a slender body equipped with a single dorsal fin and a long tail fin.
This shark also possessed a very elongate anal fin, a distinct feature of its anatomy.
Its pectoral and pelvic fins were noticeably rounded in shape.
The genus Macrourogaleus was formally described by Fowler in 1947.
Macrourogaleus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, the cartilaginous fishes.
It is closely related to Paraorthacodus and is placed in the family Paraorthacodontidae, though it was formerly classified in Palaeospinacidae.
The Paleobiology Database lists Palaeospinacidae as the parent group for Macrourogaleus.
This genus of shark lived in the Late Jurassic Solnhofen Limestone.
It inhabited the waters during the Tithonian stage, between 149.2 and 145.06 million years ago.
